summary: The Future of Artificial Intelligence Innovation Act of 2026 establishes programs, standards, and research initiatives relating to artificial intelligence across federal agencies. It creates the Center for Artificial Intelligence Standards and Innovation within the National Institute of Standards and Technology, sets up interagency testbed programs for AI evaluation, fosters international coalitions, directs studies on regulatory barriers and federal prize competitions, establishes priorities for public datasets, and adds rules regarding research security and temporary fellows.

affected_groups.effect: May voluntarily participate in standards development, testing programs, testbeds, data initiatives, and prize competitions, and benefit from aggregated research information while protecting confidential business information and trade secrets.
affected_groups.group: Private sector entities, including AI developers, deployers, and companies of all sizes

affected_groups.effect: Prohibited from accessing any of the resources of the Center for Artificial Intelligence Standards and Innovation.
affected_groups.group: Entities under the ownership, control, or influence of certain foreign governments (covered nations)

affected_groups.effect: Tasked with establishing new centers, coordinating interagency testbed programs, prioritizing public data, managing prize competitions, and submitting implementation and progress reports to Congress.
affected_groups.group: Federal agencies and laboratories (such as NIST, Department of Energy, and National Science Foundation)

affected_groups.effect: Must sign a certification with the agency head confirming they will not perform inherently governmental functions, and their usage is subject to annual inspector general audits.
affected_groups.group: Temporary fellows, contractors, and consultants working for agencies under the Act

key_provisions: Establishes the Center for Artificial Intelligence Standards and Innovation within the National Institute of Standards and Technology to assist the private sector and agencies in developing voluntary best practices and assessment tools.

Establishes a joint testbed program by the Under Secretary of Commerce for Standards and Technology and the Secretary of Energy to encourage collaboration and conduct tests, evaluations, and risk assessments of AI systems.

Requires the Director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy to develop a list of priorities for federal investment in curated, publicly available federal government data for training and evaluating AI systems.

Authorizes federal agencies to establish prize competitions and grand challenges to spur research, development, and commercialization of artificial intelligence addressing specific technological hurdles.
Directs the Comptroller General of the United States to conduct studies and report on regulatory impediments to AI innovation and on the efficacy of federal prize competitions.

Requires the formation of international coalitions and alliances with like-minded foreign governments to align technical standards, share data and expertise, and counter foreign adversary influence, while barring the People's Republic of China from participation under specific conditions.

Imposes research security requirements, certification rules to prevent temporary fellows from performing inherently governmental functions, and annual inspector general audits on the use of temporary fellows.
missing_information: Specific funding levels or appropriations authorized to carry out the act's programs and prizes.
Detailed criteria or lists for the initial grand challenges and dataset priorities beyond statutory guidelines.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Future of Artificial Intelligence Innovation Act of 2026 establishes programs, standards, and research initiatives relating to artificial intelligence across federal agencies. It creates the Center for Artificial Intelligence Standards and Innovation within the National Institute of Standards and Technology, sets up interagency testbed programs for AI evaluation, fosters international coalitions, directs studies on regulatory barriers and federal prize competitions, establishes priorities for public datasets, and adds rules regarding research security and temporary fellows.
summary_detail.significance: The bill creates formal federal structures, voluntary standards frameworks, interagency testbeds, public dataset priorities, and prize competitions aimed at accelerating U.S. artificial intelligence research and development. It impacts federal agency operations, technology development resources, international standards coordination, and research security oversight.
